Subject: MAP & Eval timeline — potential drift

Rishi / Laura,

Heads up — during integration testing this morning we hit a data-sanitization gating issue with our PII pipeline. Security needs an additional review (they quoted ~10 business days) which will push our acceptance eval completion out by roughly two weeks unless we find a workaround.

Impact: the MAP currently shows an eval-complete date of 4/03; realistic finish looks closer to 4/17. That cascades the go-live target and our procurement window.

Can we update the MAP with a contingency path? Specifically:
- Fast-path: Redwood Dedicated + security-side sandboxing; expedited approval if Redwood can provide isolation evidence and a short-term SLA addendum.
- Fallback: ship with a smaller model variant for initial adoption to keep the launch cadence.

I can loop in procurement / legal once we have a clear ask. Please advise earliest time you can meet tomorrow to align on options.

Thanks,
Jamie
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme Corp

Jamie — thanks for the heads up. We can move quickly on two axes: execution (Dedicated burst + isolated subnet) and scope (model variant). Preliminary assessment below.

Immediate proposals (options):
1) Expedited isolation path (fast-path) — we can provision a dedicated pool and share an evidence pack (network diagram, KV cache audit, short-term RBAC policy) within 48 hours. Cost delta estimate: +20–30% for the reserved week.
2) Scope-reduction path (fallback) — enable a distilled generation model for the first 30 days while the security review completes; preserves most UX flows but removes an advanced hallucination mitigation layer. Minimal cost impact.

I attached an updated MAP spreadsheet and a concise risk register with gating items so we can track decisions: MAP-v3.xlsx, risk_register_0321.csv (see attachments).

Proposed next steps:
- 03/22: 30-min alignment call to pick path (I can do 10:00–11:30 PT).
- If fast-path chosen: we will prepare the evidence pack + brief SLA addendum for procurement.
- If fallback chosen: we will prepare a rollback/playback plan and options for staged feature gating.

I'll also include a one-pager for exec escalation if you want to request credits or a shortened approval window.

—Rishi
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Appreciate the thorough options. We want to avoid pushing the launch if possible — can Redwood escalate an exec-level ask to speed procurement? Two concrete items from my side:

1) If you can provide the evidence pack and an SLA addendum language, I will push procurement to sign within 48–72 hours. DocuSign link (placeholder for when legal approves): https://docusign.com/ACME-114

If you can escalate a short exec note (1-paragraph ask + impact quant), I will present it to my VP tomorrow at 9:00 PT.

Thanks,
Jamie

On a practical note: I'd prefer the baseline MAP remain editable for both teams so we can track the chosen lane and the gating artifacts.

Summary: Acme hit a security gating item that risks a ~2-week drift in eval completion. They prefer fast-path but are willing to accept fallback if we can offer a credit. They need an exec-level one-paragraph ask to present to their VP tomorrow.

Decisions / Asks:
- Marissa: draft a one-paragraph exec escalation (impact + ask for expedited procurement + suggested credit language). Aim for a 100–150 word note. Please loop legal for the DocuSign addendum language.
- Priyom: prepare the evidence pack (network diagram, isolation controls, RBAC snapshot) and the short SLA addendum draft. Target: 03/30 12:00 PT for internal review. Attachments: slip-risk-log-0329.csv (I compiled current gating items).
- Laura: set the MAP (shared Google Sheet) to 'editable by both teams' and add the decision table row (fast-path vs fallback) with acceptance criteria.
- I will open an internal exec thread with sales leadership and include a recommended credit (one week of usage credit) so we have an approval channel if Acme pushes for it. HubSpot deal updated: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/ACME-114

I'll also include the risk register and MAP-v3.xlsx in the sales folder for visibility. We need to keep this tight—Acme's VP review is tomorrow morning.
